title: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity
authors: McCulloch WS, Pitts W
summary: Modeled neurons as binary threshold logic units and showed networks of them can compute logical functions, founding the theory of artificial neural networks.

title: Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine
authors: Wiener N
summary: Founded cybernetics, framing feedback, control and information processing as common principles of animals and machines and shaping early neural-network research.

title: The Organization of Behavior: A Neuropsychological Theory
authors: Hebb DO
summary: Proposed that synapses strengthen when pre- and post-synaptic neurons fire together (Hebbian learning), the first influential learning rule for neural networks.

title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
authors: Rosenblatt F
summary: Introduced the perceptron, a trainable threshold unit with an error-correcting learning rule and convergence guarantees for linearly separable data.

title: Adaptive Switching Circuits
authors: Widrow B, Hoff ME
summary: Introduced ADALINE and the least-mean-squares (delta) rule, gradient descent on a squared error that prefigures modern training.

title: Perceptrons: An Introduction to Computational Geometry
authors: Minsky M, Papert S
summary: Rigorously analyzed the limits of single-layer perceptrons (e.g., parity, XOR, connectedness), contributing to a long decline in neural-network funding.

title: Neural Networks and Physical Systems with Emergent Collective Computational Abilities
authors: Hopfield JJ
summary: Introduced Hopfield networks: recurrent networks with an energy function that act as content-addressable memories, linking neural computation to statistical physics.

title: A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines
authors: Ackley DH, Hinton GE, Sejnowski TJ
summary: Introduced Boltzmann machines, stochastic networks with hidden units trained by a local learning rule, an early probabilistic generative neural model.

title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2024: for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks
authors: Hopfield JJ, Hinton GE
summary: The physics Nobel recognized Hopfield networks and Boltzmann machines as foundations of modern machine learning.

title: A Stochastic Approximation Method
authors: Robbins H, Monro S
summary: Introduced stochastic approximation, the mathematical basis of stochastic gradient descent used to train virtually all neural networks.

title: The Representation of the Cumulative Rounding Error of an Algorithm as a Taylor Expansion of the Local Rounding Errors
authors: Linnainmaa S
summary: First description of reverse-mode automatic differentiation, the general algorithm underlying backpropagation.

title: Beyond Regression: New Tools for Prediction and Analysis in the Behavioral Sciences
authors: Werbos PJ
summary: Proposed applying reverse-mode gradient computation to train multilayer neural networks, an early formulation of backpropagation.

title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
authors: Rumelhart DE, Hinton GE, Williams RJ
summary: Demonstrated that backpropagation trains multilayer networks to learn useful internal representations, overcoming perceptron limitations and reviving the field.

title: Learning Long-Term Dependencies with Gradient Descent is Difficult
authors: Bengio Y, Simard P, Frasconi P
summary: Analyzed vanishing and exploding gradients in recurrent networks, explaining why long-range dependencies are hard to learn.

title: Efficient BackProp
authors: LeCun Y, Bottou L, Orr GB, Müller KR
venue: Neural Networks: Tricks of the Trade, Springer LNCS 1524
summary: Collected practical recipes for training networks: input normalization, weight initialization, sigmoid choice and learning-rate selection.

title: Understanding the Difficulty of Training Deep Feedforward Neural Networks
authors: Glorot X, Bengio Y
summary: Studied activation and gradient statistics in deep nets and proposed normalized (Xavier) initialization, enabling deep training without pretraining.

title: Adaptive Subgradient Methods for Online Learning and Stochastic Optimization
authors: Duchi J, Hazan E, Singer Y
summary: Introduced AdaGrad, per-parameter adaptive learning rates from accumulated squared gradients, the ancestor of RMSProp and Adam.

title: On the Importance of Initialization and Momentum in Deep Learning
authors: Sutskever I, Martens J, Dahl G, Hinton G
summary: Showed that careful initialization with (Nesterov) momentum SGD can train deep and recurrent networks without pretraining.

title: On the Difficulty of Training Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Pascanu R, Mikolov T, Bengio Y
summary: Analyzed exploding/vanishing gradients geometrically and introduced gradient-norm clipping, now standard practice.

title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
authors: Srivastava N, Hinton G, Krizhevsky A, Sutskever I, Salakhutdinov R
summary: Full treatment of dropout as an efficient approximate ensemble regularizer, a key ingredient of the deep-learning breakthrough.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
authors: Kingma DP, Ba J
summary: Combined momentum with RMSProp-style adaptive scaling and bias correction; became the default optimizer in deep learning.

title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
authors: Ioffe S, Szegedy C
summary: Normalized activations with mini-batch statistics, enabling higher learning rates and much faster, more stable training of deep networks.

title: Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification
authors: He K, Zhang X, Ren S, Sun J
summary: Derived variance-preserving (He/Kaiming) initialization for ReLU networks and introduced PReLU.

title: Layer Normalization
authors: Ba JL, Kiros JR, Hinton GE
summary: Normalized across features within each example instead of across the batch, making normalization usable in RNNs and later standard in Transformers.

title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
authors: Loshchilov I, Hutter F
summary: Introduced AdamW, decoupling weight decay from adaptive gradient updates; the standard optimizer for training Transformers and LLMs.

title: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
authors: Yang G, Hu EJ, Babuschkin I, Sidor S, Liu X, Farhi D, et al.
summary: Introduced the Maximal Update Parametrization (muP), under which optimal hyperparameters transfer from small to large models.

title: Muon: An Optimizer for Hidden Layers in Neural Networks
authors: Jordan K, et al.
summary: Introduced Muon, which orthogonalizes momentum updates for matrix parameters via Newton-Schulz iteration; adopted for large-scale LLM pretraining in 2025.

title: Neocognitron: A Self-Organizing Neural Network Model for a Mechanism of Pattern Recognition Unaffected by Shift in Position
authors: Fukushima K
summary: Hierarchical network of alternating feature-extracting and pooling layers inspired by visual cortex; the architectural precursor of convolutional networks.

title: Finding Structure in Time
authors: Elman JL
summary: Introduced the simple recurrent (Elman) network with context units and showed it learns temporal and grammatical structure.

title: Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts
authors: Jacobs RA, Jordan MI, Nowlan SJ, Hinton GE
summary: Introduced mixture of experts: a gating network routes inputs to specialized expert networks, the ancestor of sparse MoE layers.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
authors: Hochreiter S, Schmidhuber J
summary: Introduced the LSTM cell with gated constant-error carousels that overcome vanishing gradients, dominating sequence modeling for two decades.

title: Rectified Linear Units Improve Restricted Boltzmann Machines
authors: Nair V, Hinton GE
summary: Introduced rectified linear units for RBMs; ReLU became the default activation enabling training of deep networks.

title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
authors: Cho K, van Merriënboer B, Gulcehre C, Bahdanau D, Bougares F, Schwenk H, et al.
summary: Introduced the RNN encoder-decoder and the gated recurrent unit (GRU), a simpler alternative to LSTM.

title: Highway Networks
authors: Srivastava RK, Greff K, Schmidhuber J
summary: Used LSTM-style gates on feedforward skip connections to train networks hundreds of layers deep, anticipating residual networks.

title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
authors: Shazeer N, Mirhoseini A, Maziarz K, Davis A, Le Q, Hinton G, et al.
summary: Introduced sparsely-gated MoE layers with thousands of experts, decoupling parameter count from compute and enabling conditional computation at scale.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Chen RTQ, Rubanova Y, Bettencourt J, Duvenaud D
summary: Treated network depth as continuous time, parameterizing hidden-state derivatives with a network and training via the adjoint method.

title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
authors: Gu A, Goel K, Ré C
summary: Introduced S4, a structured state-space sequence layer with efficient convolutional computation that excelled at very long-range dependencies.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
authors: Fedus W, Zoph B, Shazeer N
summary: Simplified MoE to top-1 routing, training trillion-parameter sparse models with large speedups over dense baselines.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
authors: Gu A, Dao T
summary: Made state-space parameters input-dependent (selective) with a hardware-aware scan, matching Transformers on language at linear cost in sequence length.

title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
authors: Dao T, Gu A
summary: Showed a duality between selective SSMs and structured masked attention, yielding the faster Mamba-2 architecture.

title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
authors: Beck M, Pöppel K, Spanring M, Auer A, Prudnikova O, Kopp M, et al.
summary: Revived LSTMs at LLM scale with exponential gating and matrix memory, competing with Transformers and SSMs.

title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
authors: Liu Z, Wang Y, Vaidya S, Ruehle F, Halverson J, Soljačić M, et al.
summary: Proposed networks with learnable spline activation functions on edges, inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, as an interpretable alternative to MLPs.

title: Training Products of Experts by Minimizing Contrastive Divergence
authors: Hinton GE
summary: Introduced contrastive divergence, an efficient approximate learning rule that made training restricted Boltzmann machines practical.

title: A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets
authors: Hinton GE, Osindero S, Teh YW
summary: Showed deep belief networks can be trained greedily layer by layer as stacked RBMs, sparking the deep-learning renaissance.

title: Reducing the Dimensionality of Data with Neural Networks
authors: Hinton GE, Salakhutdinov RR
summary: Used RBM pretraining to train deep autoencoders that learn low-dimensional codes far better than PCA.

title: Extracting and Composing Robust Features with Denoising Autoencoders
authors: Vincent P, Larochelle H, Bengio Y, Manzagol PA
summary: Introduced denoising autoencoders, which learn robust representations by reconstructing clean inputs from corrupted ones; a conceptual ancestor of diffusion and masked modeling.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
authors: Kingma DP, Welling M
summary: Introduced the variational autoencoder and the reparameterization trick for scalable gradient-based variational inference in deep latent-variable models.

title: Generative Adversarial Nets
authors: Goodfellow IJ, Pouget-Abadie J, Mirza M, Xu B, Warde-Farley D, Ozair S, et al.
summary: Introduced GANs, training a generator against a discriminator in a minimax game, which led to dramatic advances in image synthesis.

title: NICE: Non-linear Independent Components Estimation
authors: Dinh L, Krueger D, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced invertible additive coupling layers with tractable Jacobians, launching normalizing-flow generative models.

title: Variational Inference with Normalizing Flows
authors: Rezende DJ, Mohamed S
summary: Introduced normalizing flows: chains of invertible transformations that build flexible distributions with tractable densities.

title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
authors: Sohl-Dickstein J, Weiss E, Maheswaranathan N, Ganguli S
summary: Introduced diffusion probabilistic models: learn to reverse a gradual noising process, the origin of modern diffusion models.

title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Radford A, Metz L, Chintala S
summary: DCGAN: architectural guidelines that made convolutional GANs train stably and revealed meaningful latent-space arithmetic.

title: Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Arjovsky M, Chintala S, Bottou L
summary: Reformulated GAN training with the Wasserstein distance, improving stability and providing a meaningful loss.

title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
authors: van den Oord A, Vinyals O, Kavukcuoglu K
summary: Introduced VQ-VAE, learning discrete latent codes via vector quantization, later central to tokenized image and audio generation.

title: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution
authors: Song Y, Ermon S
summary: Introduced noise-conditional score networks sampled with annealed Langevin dynamics, establishing score-based generative modeling.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
authors: Ho J, Jain A, Abbeel P
summary: Simplified diffusion training to a noise-prediction objective and achieved high-quality image synthesis, triggering the diffusion boom.

title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
authors: Song Y, Sohl-Dickstein J, Kingma DP, Kumar A, Ermon S, Poole B
summary: Unified score matching and diffusion as continuous-time SDEs, introducing probability-flow ODEs and exact likelihoods.

title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
authors: Dhariwal P, Nichol A
summary: Architecture improvements and classifier guidance let diffusion models surpass GANs on ImageNet sample quality.

title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
authors: Lipman Y, Chen RTQ, Ben-Hamu H, Nickel M, Le M
summary: Simulation-free training of continuous normalizing flows by regressing conditional vector fields, generalizing diffusion and now widely used.

title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
authors: Peebles W, Xie S
summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiT) replaced U-Nets with Transformers on latent patches, showing favorable scaling; the backbone of later video and image generators.

title: Consistency Models
authors: Song Y, Dhariwal P, Chen M, Sutskever I
summary: Learned to map any point on a probability-flow ODE trajectory to its origin, enabling one- or few-step generation.

title: Simplifying, Stabilizing and Scaling Continuous-Time Consistency Models
authors: Lu C, Song Y
summary: sCM: stabilized continuous-time consistency training and scaled it to billion-parameter models for two-step generation.

title: Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling
authors: Geng Z, Deng M, Bai X, Kolter JZ, He K
summary: Models average rather than instantaneous velocity fields, achieving strong one-step generation trained from scratch.

title: Approximation by Superpositions of a Sigmoidal Function
authors: Cybenko G
venue: Mathematics of Control, Signals and Systems 2:303-314
summary: Proved single-hidden-layer networks with sigmoidal units can approximate any continuous function on a compact set (universal approximation).

title: Multilayer Feedforward Networks are Universal Approximators
authors: Hornik K, Stinchcombe M, White H
summary: Established universal approximation for multilayer feedforward networks with general squashing activations.

title: Deep Learning
authors: Goodfellow I, Bengio Y, Courville A
summary: The standard textbook consolidating the theory and practice of modern deep learning.

title: Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
authors: Zhang C, Bengio S, Hardt M, Recht B, Vinyals O
summary: Showed deep nets can fit random labels, challenging classical capacity-based explanations of generalization.

title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
authors: Hestness J, Narang S, Ardalani N, Diamos G, Jun H, Kianinejad H, et al.
summary: Found power-law relationships between generalization error and dataset/model size across domains, prefiguring neural scaling laws.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
authors: Jacot A, Gabriel F, Hongler C
summary: Showed infinitely wide networks trained by gradient descent behave as kernel regression with the neural tangent kernel.

title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
authors: Frankle J, Carbin M
summary: Showed dense networks contain sparse subnetworks that, from their original initialization, train to full accuracy.

title: Reconciling Modern Machine-Learning Practice and the Classical Bias-Variance Trade-off
authors: Belkin M, Hsu D, Ma S, Mandal S
summary: Identified the double-descent risk curve, in which test error falls again beyond the interpolation threshold.

title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
authors: Nakkiran P, Kaplun G, Bansal Y, Yang T, Barak B, Sutskever I
summary: Showed model-wise, epoch-wise and sample-wise double descent across modern deep architectures.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
authors: Kaplan J, McCandlish S, Henighan T, Brown TB, Chess B, Child R, et al.
summary: Found smooth power laws relating language-model loss to parameters, data and compute, guiding the scale-up of LLMs.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
authors: Olah C, Cammarata N, Schubert L, Goh G, Petrov M, Carter S
summary: Articulated the circuits program of mechanistic interpretability: features and circuits as fundamental, reverse-engineerable units of networks.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
authors: Elhage N, Nanda N, Olsson C, Henighan T, Joseph N, Mann B, et al.
summary: Decomposed attention-only Transformers into interpretable paths, identifying induction heads and founding transformer mechanistic interpretability.

title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
authors: Power A, Burda Y, Edwards H, Babuschkin I, Misra V
summary: Discovered grokking: networks generalize long after overfitting small algorithmic tasks.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
authors: Hoffmann J, Borgeaud S, Mensch A, Buchatskaya E, Cai T, Rutherford E, et al.
summary: Chinchilla: showed parameters and training tokens should scale equally with compute, revealing earlier LLMs as undertrained.

title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
authors: Wei J, Tay Y, Bommasani R, Raffel C, Zoph B, Borgeaud S, et al.
summary: Catalogued abilities that appear abruptly only above certain model scales, influencing debate on scaling.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
authors: Elhage N, Hume T, Olsson C, Schiefer N, Henighan T, Kravec S, et al.
summary: Showed networks represent more features than dimensions via superposition, explaining polysemantic neurons.

title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
authors: Schaeffer R, Miranda B, Koyejo S
summary: Argued many emergent abilities are artifacts of discontinuous evaluation metrics rather than abrupt capability changes.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
authors: Bricken T, Templeton A, Batson J, Chen B, Jermyn A, Conerly T, et al.
summary: Used sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable monosemantic features from superposed transformer activations.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
authors: Snell C, Lee J, Xu K, Kumar A
summary: Studied compute-optimal allocation of inference-time computation, showing test-time scaling can substitute for larger models.

title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
authors: Lindsey J, Gurnee W, Ameisen E, Chen B, Pearce A, Turner NL, et al.
summary: Used attribution graphs over replacement models to trace internal multi-step reasoning and planning circuits in a production LLM.

title: The Graph Neural Network Model
authors: Scarselli F, Gori M, Tsoi AC, Hagenbuchner M, Monfardini G
summary: Full formulation of GNNs as contraction-map message passing over graphs trained by gradient descent; the origin of graph deep learning.

title: Spectral Networks and Locally Connected Networks on Graphs
authors: Bruna J, Zaremba W, Szlam A, LeCun Y
summary: Generalized convolution to graphs via the graph Laplacian spectrum, founding spectral graph convolutional networks.

title: Group Equivariant Convolutional Networks
authors: Cohen TS, Welling M
summary: Generalized convolution to symmetry groups beyond translation, founding equivariant deep learning.

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
authors: Kipf TN, Welling M
summary: Introduced the simple first-order graph convolutional network (GCN), which made GNNs practical and widely adopted.

title: Geometric Deep Learning: Going beyond Euclidean Data
authors: Bronstein MM, Bruna J, LeCun Y, Szlam A, Vandergheynst P
summary: Surveyed and named geometric deep learning: extending neural networks to graphs and manifolds.

title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
authors: Gilmer J, Schoenholz SS, Riley PF, Vinyals O, Dahl GE
summary: Unified GNN variants as message passing neural networks (MPNNs) and set state of the art on molecular property prediction.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
authors: Hamilton WL, Ying R, Leskovec J
summary: GraphSAGE: inductive node embeddings via sampled neighborhood aggregation, scaling GNNs to large evolving graphs.

title: Graph Attention Networks
authors: Veličković P, Cucurull G, Casanova A, Romero A, Liò P, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced attention-weighted neighborhood aggregation (GAT), letting GNNs learn the importance of neighbors.

title: Tensor Field Networks: Rotation- and Translation-Equivariant Neural Networks for 3D Point Clouds
authors: Thomas N, Smidt T, Kearnes S, Yang L, Li L, Kohlhoff K, et al.
summary: Built SE(3)-equivariant networks using spherical harmonics and tensor products, the basis of equivariant models for molecules.

title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
authors: Xu K, Hu W, Leskovec J, Jegelka S
summary: Related message-passing GNN expressivity to the Weisfeiler-Lehman test and proposed the maximally expressive GIN.

title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Satorras VG, Hoogeboom E, Welling M
summary: Simple E(n)-equivariant message passing on coordinates without spherical harmonics, widely used for molecules and generative modeling.

title: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
authors: Bronstein MM, Bruna J, Cohen T, Veličković P
summary: Unified CNNs, GNNs, Transformers and equivariant networks under a symmetry and invariance-based blueprint.

title: Learning Skillful Medium-Range Global Weather Forecasting
authors: Lam R, Sanchez-Gonzalez A, Willson M, Wirnsberger P, Fortunato M, Alet F, et al.
summary: GraphCast: a mesh-based GNN that outperformed leading numerical weather prediction on 10-day forecasts.

title: GPU Implementation of Neural Networks
authors: Oh KS, Jung K
summary: Early demonstration of accelerating neural-network inference on graphics hardware.

title: Scalable Parallel Programming with CUDA
authors: Nickolls J, Buck I, Garland M, Skadron K
summary: Described NVIDIA's CUDA model for general-purpose GPU programming, the platform on which deep learning computation was built.

title: Large-scale Deep Unsupervised Learning using Graphics Processors
authors: Raina R, Madhavan A, Ng AY
summary: Showed GPUs speed up training of deep belief nets and sparse coding by up to 70x, pointing the way to GPU-based deep learning.

title: Theano: A CPU and GPU Math Compiler in Python
authors: Bergstra J, Breuleux O, Bastien F, Lamblin P, Pascanu R, Desjardins G, et al.
venue: Proceedings of the 9th Python in Science Conference (SciPy 2010)
summary: Pioneered symbolic computation graphs with automatic differentiation compiled to GPU, the template for later deep-learning frameworks.

title: cuDNN: Efficient Primitives for Deep Learning
authors: Chetlur S, Woolley C, Vandermersch P, Cohen J, Tran J, Catanzaro B, et al.
summary: NVIDIA's library of optimized GPU deep-learning kernels, underpinning nearly all frameworks.

title: TensorFlow: A System for Large-Scale Machine Learning
authors: Abadi M, Barham P, Chen J, Chen Z, Davis A, Dean J, et al.
summary: Google's dataflow-graph framework for training and deploying models across heterogeneous devices at scale.

title: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit
authors: Jouppi NP, Young C, Patil N, Patterson D, Agrawal G, Bajwa R, et al.
summary: Described Google's TPU, a systolic-array ASIC for neural networks, launching the era of specialized AI accelerators.

title: Mixed Precision Training
authors: Micikevicius P, Narang S, Alben J, Diamos G, Elsen E, Garcia D, et al.
summary: Trained networks in FP16 with FP32 master weights and loss scaling, halving memory and exploiting tensor cores.

title: JAX: Composable Transformations of Python+NumPy Programs
authors: Bradbury J, Frostig R, Hawkins P, Johnson MJ, Leary C, Maclaurin D, et al.
summary: Composable function transformations (grad, jit, vmap, pmap) compiled via XLA; widely used for large-scale research on TPUs and GPUs.

title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
authors: Shoeybi M, Patwary M, Puri R, LeGresley P, Casper J, Catanzaro B
summary: Efficient intra-layer tensor parallelism for Transformers, a cornerstone of large-scale LLM training.

title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
authors: Paszke A, Gross S, Massa F, Lerer A, Bradbury J, Chanan G, et al.
summary: Define-by-run framework with eager execution and dynamic autograd that became the dominant deep-learning library.

title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
authors: Rajbhandari S, Rasley J, Ruwase O, He Y
summary: Partitioned optimizer states, gradients and parameters across data-parallel workers (DeepSpeed), removing memory redundancy.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
authors: Dao T, Fu DY, Ermon S, Rudra A, Ré C
summary: IO-aware tiled exact attention that avoids materializing the attention matrix, greatly speeding up Transformers and enabling long contexts.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
authors: DeepSeek-AI
summary: 671B-parameter MoE model trained at low cost using FP8 mixed precision, multi-head latent attention and communication-overlapping pipeline parallelism.
